items.title: Kiro apps now speak 13 languages
items.summary:
Three Kiro apps now follow your system language: Ohmychadwm Tweak Tool, Alacritty Tweak Tool and KiroTux Drive.

  • Languages: Dutch, German, Spanish, French, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Hungarian, Italian, Turkish, Polish, Japanese, Chinese (simplified) and Romanian, besides English. Portugal gets Brazilian Portuguese, Taiwan and Hong Kong simplified Chinese.
  • Every app has a language dropdown: pick another language there and press Restart now. In Ohmychadwm Tweak Tool it sits under Status, in the other two at the top of the window.
  • The menu entries are translated too.

The Kiro website speaks eight languages as well: pick yours in the language menu at the top of kiroproject.be.

You get the new versions with your next sudo pacman -Syu. More Kiro apps follow.

items.title: KiroTux Wayfire v26.10.23 is out
items.summary:
A fifth KiroTux edition is available: KiroTux Wayfire v26.10.23.

KiroTux is built on Kiro, with the same packages, repositories and rolling Arch Linux base. It is put together and tested as one ISO for one Wayland desktop: here Wayfire, a compositor with real 3D effects (desktop cube, an overview of every workspace, wobbly windows, blur and zoom), with waybar. Windows tile by themselves, and the bar, notifications and terminal take their colours from your wallpaper: Alt + N gives you a new wallpaper and the desktop recolours with it.

It comes with Kirotux Wayfire Premium (Ctrl + Alt + H), a settings app made for Wayfire:

  • Theme, icons, cursor and font; Light or Dark recolours your apps, waybar, the notifications and Alacritty together
  • Window style: borders, gaps, blur and the open/close animations
  • Wallpapers, keyboard layouts and one-click looks, with Undo
  • Displays, mouse and touchpad, power and night light
  • Default apps, startup apps and which screen an app opens on

The desktop config itself, kiro-wayfire, stays free on Kiro.

KiroTux works with donations: you choose the amount, above a minimum donation.

items.title: Kiro ISO Builder: see what your ISO ships before you build it
items.summary:
The Kiro ISO Builder has a new release, the version we've been testing in the beta builder.

The biggest change: you can see what your ISO will contain before you build it. The package page is much clearer. Packages are grouped into sections you can open and close, each with a count. Packages that always ship are no longer mixed in with the ones you can choose, and if you untick one that comes back anyway because another app needs it, the builder marks it.

Each desktop now has its own optional extras. With XFCE you can drop the text editor, the music player or the image viewer and keep the rest. The parts the panel needs, like the menu and the volume control, can't be unticked any more.

On the build page, a summary shows what will be removed, what stays and what gets pulled in, with the reasons. Every time you start a build, the builder saves that summary with the date and time in ~/.config/kiro-iso-builder/, so you can look back at what went into each ISO.

You also choose which desktop the installed system logs into first, and the login screen is cleaner: each desktop appears once.

Tested from start to finish: an ISO built from the script and one built with the builder, both live and installed. To get it, just update your system: sudo pacman -Syu

Watch the video · Kiro ISO Builder on GitHub

items.title: Qtile users: do not upgrade python-xcffib to 1.7.0
items.summary:
Arch's python-xcffib 1.7.0-1 (15 October) breaks Qtile. After the upgrade Qtile no longer starts, on X11 or Wayland: you get a black screen or land back on the login screen, and Qtile's log stays empty. This affects every Arch-based system with Qtile, not only Kiro.

Not upgraded yet? Hold it back for now: sudo pacman -Syu --ignore python-xcffib

Already upgraded? Log in to another session or a TTY (Ctrl + Alt + F3) and go back to 1.6.2:

sudo pacman -U https://archive.archlinux.org/packages/p/python-xcffib/python-xcffib-1.6.2-1-any.pkg.tar.zst

Then add IgnorePkg = python-xcffib to /etc/pacman.conf so the next update doesn't bring 1.7.0 back. Remove that line again once Arch ships a newer python-xcffib: the bug is fixed upstream in 1.7.1.

Watch the video · Qtile bug report · Arch bug report

items.title: Next release v26.10.01 ships linux as the main kernel and linux-lts as backup
items.summary:
The next Kiro ISO, v26.10.01, is due on 1 October 2026 and it changes the kernel pairing:

  • linux, the plain, official Arch kernel, becomes the one you boot by default
  • linux-lts is installed alongside it as the backup

Every monthly Kiro ISO ships two kernels on purpose: one that boots by default and a second one that is installed as well, so a bad kernel update never leaves you without something to boot. Both kernels and their matching -headers survive the install, so DKMS modules (VirtualBox guest additions, NVIDIA) stay buildable for both.

The pairing is deliberately rotated month to month. v26.09.01 shipped linux-cachyos with linux-zen. Rotating keeps the other kernels genuinely exercised on real installs instead of only in theory.

Nothing to do on your current system: this is about what a fresh install from the October ISO gives you. If you want the LTS kernel on an existing Kiro machine, add it yourself with sudo pacman -S linux-lts linux-lts-headers.

items.title: Why pacman may warn broadcom-wl-dkms local is newer than extra
items.summary:
If you have the optional cachyos repository enabled and see a warning like warning: broadcom-wl-dkms: local (6.30.223.271-49) is newer than extra (6.30.223.271-48), this is expected and not a bug.

cachyos rebuilds some packages, including DKMS driver packages like broadcom-wl-dkms, on its own schedule. It can ship a higher pkgrel than the current extra build before Arch's own rebuild catches up. Kiro's /etc/pacman.conf lists extra before cachyos, so once you're on the cachyos build, later syncs keep resolving against extra's (older) pkgrel, and pacman flags the mismatch rather than silently downgrading you.

There is nothing to fix. pacman will not downgrade an installed package on its own, so your working driver stays installed. The warning clears itself once extra publishes a pkgrel that catches up with or exceeds cachyos's.

If you'd rather not see it:

  • pin the package to extra with a [options] NoUpgrade = broadcom-wl-dkms line, or
  • simply ignore the warning: it's cosmetic.

items.title: New app: Fish Tweak Tool
items.summary:
Say hello to Fish Tweak Tool, a GTK4 graphical configurator for the fish shell.

Fish already ships a theme picker, but it can't install prompts and plugins for you. This app fills that gap:

  • install a modern prompt: Tide, Starship, Hydro, Pure
  • toggle the must-have fisher plugins
  • browse colour themes
  • tune the greeting and cursor

All from one desktop app, with no browser and no sudo. It only ever writes per-user overrides to ~/.config/fish/, so it never fights the shipped Kiro defaults.

Install it with sudo pacman -S fish-tweak-tool. Fish Tweak Tool on GitHub

items.title: Check your /etc/pacman.conf has the Kiro repositories
items.summary:
Make sure your /etc/pacman.conf enables the repositories Kiro relies on:

  • nemesis_repo: Kiro's own packages
  • chaotic-aur
  • cachyos: optional, shipped disabled

If any are missing, open the file as root and add these blocks:

[nemesis_repo]
Include = /etc/pacman.d/kiro-mirrorlist

[chaotic-aur]
Include = /etc/pacman.d/chaotic-mirrorlist

#[cachyos]
#Include = /etc/pacman.d/cachyos-mirrorlist

Then refresh with sudo pacman -Syu.

cachyos is shown commented out: it is disabled by default on Kiro (chaotic-aur is the backstop). Uncomment it only if you want it.

Fresh Kiro installs already have these set up. This is a reminder for anyone who edited pacman.conf by hand or is migrating an existing system.

items.title: Optional: pause upgrades on Arch news with informant
items.summary:
Want your system to pause before an upgrade until you've read the latest Arch news? informant is an optional tool that shows Arch announcements and holds back pacman/paru/yay until you've seen them. It's a useful safety net, especially after incidents like the recent AUR one.

It is opt-in and not installed by default on Kiro. To turn it on:

  • paru -S informant (it's in chaotic-aur, already enabled on Kiro)
  • then run informant read to clear the current news

You can remove it any time with paru -R informant. informant in the AUR

items.title: Kiro is not affected by the AUR malicious-packages incident
items.summary:
Arch has posted a security advisory about a wave of malicious package uploads to the AUR.

Kiro is not affected. Its installer and tooling install packages only from the official Arch repositories and from chaotic-aur, a signed, centrally built binary repo. Nothing Kiro ships pulls or builds packages straight from the AUR, and we audited our install scripts after the advisory with no exposure.

If you install AUR packages yourself with yay, paru or by hand, the usual Arch advice applies: review every PKGBUILD and .install script before you build, especially right now. The AUR is user-submitted and unsigned, so that trust step is always yours.

There is nothing you need to do on Kiro itself. Read the Arch advisory
